newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senator says high service costs hurt residents.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senator says high service costs hurt residents.

text.p: New York State Senator Franz Leichter (D-Manhattan) said on Tuesday that the costs of service increases outweighed the benefits of the first year of tax cuts put in place by the Republican Pataki Administration.
In 1995, income tax cuts saved residents $515 million, but increases in local fees, fares, tolls and tuition cost them $1.54 billion, Leichter said, in prepared remarks.
The study by Leichter found that in counties, cities, not including New York City, towns and villages, local revenue from fees and fines rose by $933 million or six percent.
In New York City, revenues from fees and fines rose seven percent in 1995.
"Gov. Pataki's vaunted tax cuts have done nothing but shift the revenue burden to localities," Leichter said.
